title: Rollback Policy Weaver: declarative canaries with hysteresis, risk budget, and temporal slicing
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Summary:
Build a declarative policy engine ("Rollback Policy Weaver") that composes time-aware canary schedules, step-based traffic splits, and safety guardrails into a single runtime-configurable artifact. The engine's goals are: reduce manual intervention during rollouts, provide deterministic hysteresis around noisy metrics, bind risk budgets to traffic exposure, and enable automated, explainable rollbacks when regressions are detected.

Problem:
Current canary tooling requires many brittle scripts and ad-hoc heuristics in the control plane. Rollouts are vulnerable to short-term metric spikes, lacking hysteresis (we flip traffic on a single spike), and we have no standard way to cap cumulative exposure to risky models (no risk budget). This causes customer impact and manual toil during incidents.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals: declarative policies for step schedules, built-in hysteresis windows, risk-budget accounting, time-sliced shadow probing, rollback reasonability explanations, and tight integration with Console telemetry and runbooks.
- Non-goals: automated model selection, full A/B statistical hypothesis testing engine (we will integrate with existing eval pipelines later).

Design sketch:
- Policy format: YAML/JSON schema with top-level fields: name, traffic_steps (list), metrics (list of KPI thresholds), hysteresis (window in minutes + smoothing), risk_budget (tokens), rollback_rules (hard thresholds + trend rules), and probes (shadow routes + sample_pct).
- Scheduler: translates traffic_steps into a step timeline with absolute or relative times, supports dynamic backoffs (exponential or linear) when hysteresis fails.
- Hysteresis: every KPI has a lookback window and an aggregation function (p95, rate, moving_avg). Changes only count after the window is satisfied for N consecutive windows.
- Risk budget: each policy has a numeric budget representing maximum allowed user-exposure minutes for the canary. Failed steps deduct tokens; safe progress refunds a fraction. The budget prevents runaway exposure even if operators forget to stop a rollout.
- Temporal slicing: supports scheduling windows by timezone and traffic carveouts (e.g., 10% during peak hours, 30% off-peak) and enables shadow probing during low traffic slices.
- Rollback reasons: policies emit structured explanations ("p95_latency_up_>+50%_over_5m", "error_rate_>0.5%_sustained") stored as short strings so Console can surface the why.

Runtime integration and APIs:
- Admin API: POST /v1/policies -> validates and activates. PATCH supports canary pause/resume/override.
- Scheduler: integrates with the routing mesh to program traffic split directives (weight configs) and to the shadow proxy for probe routes.
- Telemetry: emit events to Console: policy.activate, step.start, step.complete, step.fail, rollback.triggered with reason and metadata. Use existing tracing headers to link requests to policy events.

Safety & testing:
- Unit tests for policy compiler and hysteresis math.
- Integration tests with a local routing shim that simulates latency/error deltas and validates rollback triggers.
- Chaos test: inject transient spikes to ensure hysteresis prevents unnecessary rollbacks.

Config example (YAML):
name: "weave-sms-model-v2-canary"
traffic_steps:
  - step: 1
    target_percent: 2
    min_duration: 10m
  - step: 2
    target_percent: 10
    min_duration: 30m
hysteresis:
  p95_latency:
    lookback: 5m
    windows: 3
    agg: moving_avg
risk_budget:
  tokens: 180  # minutes of user exposure cap
rollback_rules:
  - metric: error_rate
    comparator: ">"
    threshold: "0.5%"
    sustained: 5m
  - metric: p95_latency
    comparator: ">"
    threshold: "+40%"
    sustained: 15m
probes:
  shadow_percentage: 1
  endpoints: ["/classify","/embed"]

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy schema validated by JSON Schema + unit tests.
- End-to-end flow that: activates a policy, executes steps, detects a regression with hysteresis, and triggers an automated rollback with a clear reason observable in Console.
- Risk budget enforcement halts progress when consumed.
- Docs for PM/Operators: how to author policies, risk budgeting guidance, and runbook examples.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Aggressive hysteresis prevents churn but delays rollout detection for real regressions; choose defaults conservatively (short windows for high-risk customers).
- Risk budget accounting model (deduct vs. continuous) — proposed deduct-on-exposure-minute for simplicity.
- Should we offer a "dry-run" mode that simulates a policy without changing traffic? (recommended, MVP: yes)

Rollout plan:
1) Implement policy compiler + JSON Schema (backend)
2) Wire scheduler to route service in staging (non-customer traffic)
3) Add Console views for policy status and audit logs
4) Canary with internal teams, iterate on hysteresis defaults
5) GA with docs and prebuilt policy templates
comments: 2025-02-16: Kickoff meeting with PM and Console team. Decided to prioritize risk budget primitives and hysteresis in the first iteration. Action: Ava to prototype policy schema.
2025-02-18: Design feedback from Sophie Patel (Product): require 'dry_run' flag and human-override endpoints. Added to API surface.
2025-02-20: Marcus implemented initial JSON Schema and small compiler. Local unit tests passing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1248
2025-02-24: Integration test failing intermittently under simulated traffic spikes — increased default hysteresis windows from 2x to 3x. Filed follow-up ENG-87400 to tune per-customer defaults.
2025-02-28: Security review triage: no high-risk surface, but auditing must be enabled for policy changes (Console event). Security note added to docs.
